newsitem.title: GERMANY: Majority of Germans opposed to euro, survey finds.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Germans opposed to euro, survey finds.

text.p: A slim majority of Germans is against the planned single European currency with the strongest opposition coming from eastern Germany and left-leaning voters, a survey by the Forsa institute published on Saturday found.
The survey of 1,011 Germans by the Forsa research institute for RTL television found that 51 percent opposed the euro's introduction while 34 percent were in favour.

In formerly communist eastern Germany, 55 percent said they were against the euro and only 26 percent were in favour. Among supporters of the left-leaning Social Democrats (SPD), 57 percent opposed the euro and 30 percent were in favour.

Even backing for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from those who support Chancellor's Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats was meagre -- only 39 percent said they were in favour of the euro's introduction.
